extraction.Name: Joseph Hornbeck
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not wish it, for he did not want to pay taxes; but that the Indian Agency informed him that, if he did not take charge of the patent, and pay his taxes on the land, that land would be taxed just the same, and finally sold for same, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold his 320 acre allotment to John Hart, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $800.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: John Hart, of Rapid City, South Dakota, for $800.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: in 1920, being behind in taxes, he sold his 320 acre allotment; deponent paid the back taxes out of the $800.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: works for farmers, this being his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has pretty fair health; has a wife, two children and a grandchild to support; daughter has weak eyes and boy is not healthy; finds it pretty hard to get along on his income; did not sell his place for debts incurred prior to receiving his patent in fee; considers he received a very poor price for his land; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; forced patent in fee to 320 acres; document subscribed and sworn December 22, 1928; file reference 62420 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Pine Ridge (Shannon County, South Dakota)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
